questions.question:
Four Pods run in the namespace `spectacle`. Scan the images they use with Trivy (installed on the jumphost) and **delete the Pods whose image has vulnerabilities of severity CRITICAL**.

Pods whose image has no CRITICAL vulnerability must be kept running (a HIGH vulnerability alone is not a reason to delete a Pod).

verification.description: The Pod atlas (image with CRITICAL vulnerabilities) is deleted
The Pod beacon (image with CRITICAL vulnerabilities) is deleted
The Pods without CRITICAL vulnerabilities are kept

questions.question:
In the namespace `seminar`:

1. Create a ServiceAccount named `seminar-sa`.
2. Create a Role named `k8s-seminar` that allows **only** the operations `create` and `update`, **only** on the resources `pods` and `deployments`.
3. Create a RoleBinding named `k8s-seminar-bind` that binds the Role `k8s-seminar` to the ServiceAccount `seminar-sa`.

verification.description: ServiceAccount seminar-sa exists in seminar
Role k8s-seminar allows only create and update on pods and deployments
RoleBinding k8s-seminar-bind binds k8s-seminar to seminar-sa
seminar-sa can create and update pods and deployments in seminar, and nothing else

questions.question:
The Pod `apparmor-pod` (image `nginx:alpine`) runs on the worker node `{{NODE01}}` in the namespace `apparmor-lab`. It has two problems: it runs with **privileged** permissions, and its container can **read the files in `/data/records`**.

Fix both:

- The AppArmor profile `spectacleapp` is prepared in `/etc/apparmor.d/spectacleapp` on `{{NODE01}}`. Load it on `{{NODE01}}` and make the Pod use it, so that reading `/data/records` is denied inside the container. The web server of the Pod must keep working.
- The Pod must not be privileged.
- Create a ServiceAccount named `test-sa` in `apparmor-lab` and make the Pod use it.

The Pod must be running on `{{NODE01}}` when you are done (keep its name `apparmor-pod`).

verification.description: The AppArmor profile spectacleapp is loaded on {{NODE01}}
apparmor-pod is not privileged and uses the AppArmor profile spectacleapp
The ServiceAccount test-sa exists and apparmor-pod uses it
apparmor-pod runs, reading /data/records is denied and the web server still answers

questions.question:
In the namespace `secret-lab`:

1. Create a Secret named `secret1` with the keys `user` = `admin` and `pass` = `P455W0RD`.
2. Create a Pod named `secretpod` (image `nginx`) that mounts the Secret `secret1` as a **volume** with the `readOnly` option, in a path of your choice.

verification.description: Secret secret1 has user=admin and pass=P455W0RD
secretpod (nginx) mounts secret1 as a read-only volume
secretpod runs and the secret files are readable and read-only inside the container

questions.question:
Use a local seccomp profile for a Pod.

The profile `auditing.json` is provided on the jumphost in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-002-q5/`. The kubelet looks for local profiles in `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp` on the node that runs the Pod.

1. Install the profile on the worker node `{{NODE01}}`, under `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp` (the directory does not exist yet).
2. Create a Pod named `nginx-auditing` in the namespace `alpha`, using the `nginx` image, that runs on `{{NODE01}}` and uses this local profile in the **security context** of the Pod.

The Pod must be running.

verification.description: The provided profile is installed under /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp on {{NODE01}}
nginx-auditing (nginx) runs on {{NODE01}} with the Localhost seccomp profile
The container of nginx-auditing is running and confined by a seccomp filter

questions.question:
1. Create a RuntimeClass named `runsc-class` that uses the handler `runsc` (gVisor).
2. Create a Pod named `gvisor-pod` (image `nginx`) in the namespace `sandbox-test` that runs with this RuntimeClass.

The Pod must be running inside the gVisor sandbox (the output of `dmesg` in the container shows it).

verification.description: RuntimeClass runsc-class uses the handler runsc
gvisor-pod (nginx) uses the RuntimeClass runsc-class
gvisor-pod runs inside the gVisor sandbox
The kubelet of {{NODE01}} uses the authorization mode Webhook
The kubelet of {{NODE01}} protects the kernel defaults
The read-only port of the kubelet of {{NODE01}} is disabled

questions.question:
Enable auditing in the cluster (control plane `{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`).

Create an audit policy file `/etc/kubernetes/test-audit.yaml` that logs **only** these events:

- namespace: `test`
- level: `Metadata`
- operations: `delete` and `update`
- resources: `pods`

Everything else must not be logged. Configure the API server to use this policy, to write the audit log to `/var/log/test-audit.log` and to keep the logs for at most **20 days**. Wait until the API server is healthy again.

verification.description: kube-apiserver uses /etc/kubernetes/test-audit.yaml, a valid audit Policy
The audit log path is /var/log/test-audit.log and the retention is 20 days
Deleting and updating pods in the namespace test is logged at Metadata level
Nothing else is logged

questions.question:
A Pod in the namespace `space` (`worker-pod`, on `{{NODE02}}`) raised an alert because a shell was opened in its container. Falco runs as a service on `{{NODE02}}` (`falco-modern-bpf`, rules in `/etc/falco`).

Find the Falco rule **`Terminal shell in container`** and change its **output** so that the alert starts with these four values, in this order, separated by commas (more text may follow). Each one is the real value of the event, not the words below:

1. time in ISO 8601
2. user id
3. container id
4. container image repository

Make Falco use the changed rule (the service must be running). It is checked by opening a shell with a terminal in the Pod (`kubectl exec -it`) and reading the alert that Falco logs.

verification.description: The alert starts with the ISO 8601 timestamp
The second field of the alert is the user id
The third field of the alert is the container id
The fourth field of the alert is the container image repository

questions.question:
Deploy an **ImagePolicyWebhook** admission controller on the cluster (control plane `{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`).

The webhook backend already runs on the control plane (`https://127.0.0.1:8443/image_policy`); it rejects the images of the registry `untrusted.example.com` and accepts the others. The admission configuration `/etc/kubernetes/pki/admission_configuration.yaml` has a problem that prevents it from working (its kubeconfig is `/etc/kubernetes/pki/admission_kube_config.yaml`).

1. Fix the problem in `/etc/kubernetes/pki/admission_configuration.yaml` and make sure the policy is **implicit deny** (the images are denied when the backend cannot be reached).
2. Make sure the plugin is enabled on the kube-apiserver **in addition to** the plugins already enabled, and that the API server loads this admission configuration.

Wait until the API server is healthy again. Pods with ordinary images (for example `nginx`) must still be accepted.

verification.description: kube-apiserver enables ImagePolicyWebhook (the other plugins kept) and loads the admission configuration
The admission configuration is fixed: implicit deny and an existing kubeconfig
Images of untrusted.example.com are denied by the webhook
Pods with ordinary images are still admitted

questions.question:
PodSecurityPolicy no longer exists in Kubernetes. Implement the same restrictions with a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** for the namespace `policy-lab` only:

- Create a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy named `pod-psp` and a ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding named `pod-psp-binding` that applies it to the namespace `policy-lab` and **denies** the requests that violate it.
- Privileged containers are not allowed (init containers included).
- The only volume types allowed are `secret` and `configMap` (the `projected` volume that Kubernetes injects for the service account token must keep working).
- `runAsUser`, `fsGroup`, `seLinux` and the supplemental groups stay unrestricted.

The namespace `open-lab` must stay unrestricted.

verification.description: Policy pod-psp and binding pod-psp-binding exist (Deny)
Privileged Pods are rejected in policy-lab
policy-lab accepts secret and configMap volumes only
RunAsAny settings are accepted in policy-lab and open-lab is unaffected

questions.question:
In the namespace `moon`, create a NetworkPolicy named `np-restriction` for the Pod `nginx-pod` (port 80).

Only these sources may connect to `nginx-pod`:

- all the Pods of the namespace `hello` (look at the labels of the namespace: `kubectl get ns hello --show-labels`);
- the Pods with the label `app=backend` of **any** namespace.

All other ingress traffic to `nginx-pod` must be denied (including the other Pods of the namespace `moon`).

verification.description: NetworkPolicy np-restriction exists in moon and restricts the ingress of nginx-pod
The Pods of the namespace hello can reach nginx-pod
The Pods labelled app=backend of any namespace can reach nginx-pod
All other Pods are denied

questions.question: In the namespace `lockdown`, create a NetworkPolicy named `all-deny` that denies **all ingress and all egress** traffic of every Pod of the namespace.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy all-deny selects every Pod and denies all ingress and egress
No Pod can reach the Pod server: all ingress is denied
The Pod client cannot open any connection: all egress is denied
The base image is pinned to a specific ubuntu version
The Dockerfile ends with an unprivileged user
apt-get update and install run in one RUN instruction, wget and curl installed
The other instructions were kept
